title: Assurance narrative: inference data controls & audit log positioning
content:
Purpose:
This brief is a compact, sales- and technical-facing assurance narrative for Redwood Inference focused on: SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness, inference data handling boundaries, and clear audit-log language that can be used in seller scripts, security RFP responses, and security appendix content. It is intended to be concise enough for seller one-pagers and detailed enough to map to evidence for diligence calls.

Audience:
- Enterprise sales (pre-sign and churn-risk conversations)
- Solutions engineering and CSEs during security deep-dives
- Product marketing for compliance one-pagers
- Legal/security review teams who will map claims to artifacts

High-level positioning (one-liner for sellers):
"Redwood provides enterprise-grade inference with configurable data boundaries — hosted, dedicated, or private — plus tamper-evident audit trails and verifiable control artifacts to satisfy SOC2/ISO/HIPAA evaluations."

Key claims (short, verifiable statements to use in proposals):
- SOC2 Type II: Redwood maintains a SOC2 Type II report covering system change, access controls, logging, and incident response (report available under NDA).
- ISO alignment: Controls mapped to ISO27001 Annex A are available; customer mapping packages supplied on request.
- HIPAA readiness: Hosted and Dedicated products support PHI handling when customers choose Private deployments or enable specific PHI controls (BAA available; technical/administrative safeguards documented).
- Data residency & isolation: Customers can choose region-bound hosted endpoints, Dedicated clusters, or Private VPC/on-prem deployments for full data isolation.
- Audit log fidelity: Token-level inference events, route/model metadata, timestamps, and requester identity are recorded with configurable retention windows and export capabilities. Logs are cryptographically protected and immutability options exist for Dedicated/Private customers.

Evidence & artifacts (what sellers should offer during diligence):
- SOC2 Type II report (past 12 months) — redacted copy under NDA.
- Audit-log schema doc and sample export (CSV/JSON) showing fields and retention.
- Penetration test summary and remediation tracker.
- Data flow diagrams (hosted/dedicated/private) and KMS/HSM architecture diagram.
- BAA template for HIPAA customers, and checklist of PHI controls.
- ISO mapping table and control-owner list.

Data handling & control boundaries (explainer for engineers + buyers):
- Inference surface: Only model inputs and generated outputs touch the inference runtime. For hosted API, temporary request metadata (route, model, tenant id) is recorded for observability and billing.
- Retention & minimization: Default retention for request logs is 30 days; retention tiering policies (7/30/365/custom) available. Customers can request immediate deletion for specific datasets via support/legal workflow or choose Private deployments where logs remain under their control.
- Customer-managed encryption: KMS integration (cloud KMS or customer HSM) available for Dedicated and Private tiers; hosted customers may opt for CMEK for supported regions.
- Access controls: RBAC for console/API, SSO integration (SAML/OIDC), and fine-grained key roles for audit-log access.
- Data in transit & at rest: TLS 1.2+/AES-256 for rest; periodic cipher upgrades per crypto policy.

Audit log language — recommended boilerplate (for proposals and response templates):
"Redwood emits structured audit events for inference requests that include a non-content identifier for request correlation, route/model metadata, request timestamp, response latency, and the identifier of the requesting principal. Content payloads are not stored by default beyond the configured retention window. Audit events are tamper-evident and available for export via secure endpoints; Dedicated and Private customers can enable immutability and direct log streaming to customer-owned sinks for long-term retention."

Audit log schema summary (fields sellers should highlight):
- event_id
- tenant_id (opaque)
- route/model id/version
- timestamp
- request_latency_ms
- request_size_tokens
- response_size_tokens
- requester_principal
- action (generate, embed, rerank, cancel)
- storage_retention_tier
- export_reference (if streamed to customer sink)

Recommended claims to avoid (legal-safe phrasing):
- Avoid absolute permanence language: don’t say "immutable forever" for hosted logs. Instead: "tamper-evident; immutability options available for Dedicated/Private customers."
- Avoid implying PHI handling on hosted tier unless customer signs a BAA and configures required controls.

Competitive differentiators vs. common alternatives (talking points):
- Vs. hyperscalers: Hyperscalers offer primitives; Redwood provides model-serving-specific controls (token-aware audit fields, prefix/KV cache visibility, and inference-specific retention policies) plus a single operational experience across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Vs. LLM-API providers: Many competitors store full content for product analytics. Redwood defaults to minimized content retention and provides turnkey paths for customers who require strict isolation (Dedicated/Private + CMEK + direct log streaming).
- Vs. self-hosted runtimes: Self-hosting gives control but requires customer to build audit/export tooling. Redwood’s Dedicated/Private packages include hardened, certified controls, and an evidence bundle that accelerates vendor due diligence.

Objection handling (short — for SEs/sellers):
- "We need proof of logs and retention." -> "We can provide a sample, redacted audit export and the audit-log schema; for enterprise deals we stream logs to customer sinks or enable immutability in Dedicated/Private deployments."
- "Can you sign a BAA?" -> "Yes — BAAs are available. For PHI, we recommend Dedicated or Private so data residency, KMS, and network isolation requirements are fully met."
- "How do you prove logs weren't altered?" -> "Logs are cryptographically hashed with per-batch signing; Dedicated/Private customers can enable append-only storage to customer-owned sinks."

Seller one-pagers / soundbites (quick snippets):
- Security engineers: "We map our audit logs to SOC2 controls and can export structured events to your SIEM for correlation — sample exports available under NDA."
- Legal/compliance: "Redwood provides a SOC2 Type II report, ISO mapping, and a BAA template; our Dedicated/Private options enable customer-managed keys and log custody."
- CTO/Platform: "Choose Hosted for speed, Dedicated for guaranteed throughput/isolation, or Private for full control — all share the same runtime and audit semantics so your integration is consistent."

Evidence mapping checklist (for security/solutions engineering to gather pre-demo):
- Provide SOC2 Type II redacted report (most recent).
- Provide audit-log schema and sample export (sanitized).
- Confirm retention settings and export pipeline options for the prospect.
- Provide network topology diagram (VPC, peering, private link options).
- Provide BAA template and PHI control checklist if prospect requires HIPAA.
- Provide KMS/HSM integration whitepaper and key rotation policy.

Next steps & suggested artifacts to produce from GTM:  (priority ordering)
1) Short (1-page) "Audit log evidence" sheet with fields, sample export, and export options (hosted vs stream).
2) SOC2/ISO/Baa one-pager pack for legal teams (redacted reports + mapping).
3) Engineering FAQ for CSEs: how to enable CMEK, how to configure log streaming, timelines for immutability enables.
4) Sales play: script + objection deck for 15–30 minute security diligence calls.

Open questions (actions for Security/Product teams):
- Confirm canonical default retention for hosted logs and create templated language for NDA-era redacted report sharing.
- Finalize phraseology for "tamper-evident" (what exact cryptographic guarantees can we document publicly?).
- Document the exact export formats and sample schemas for SIEM integrations (Splunk, Datadog, ELK).

Appendix — quick FAQ (for sellers to memorize):
Q: Can you store PHI in hosted API?
A: Not recommended by default. Hosted customers must sign a BAA and implement required controls — we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments for PHI workloads.

Q: Are logs exportable to our SIEM?
A: Yes — we have secure streaming and batch export options; we can also push to customer-owned cloud storage or event bus for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Q: How long do you keep logs?
A: Default 30 days; configurable per-contract with long-term retention options on Dedicated/Private.

Q: Is your SOC2 public?
A: SOC2 Type II summary and redacted report available under NDA.

Q: Will you sign a BAA?
A: Yes, we provide a standard BAA for customers with HIPAA requirements.

Contact & owners for follow-up:
- GTM owner: Ivy Morales (owner of this brief)
- SE lead: Marco Ruiz
- Security liaison: Priya Nair

Notes on tone and use: Keep this brief as the canonical short narrative for sales and SEs. Do not overpromise — use conditional language for hosted tier and emphasize Dedicated/Private for stronger custody controls. Update this doc after the next security review to reflect exact crypto/immutability language and the latest SOC2 date.
